contract: Surface: every MAIZ Agents page: landing (/), employees and store, pricing, security, log in, 404, onboarding and all ten control center screens (/app.html). Audience: founders and small-business owners with no AI background. Job: understand what the AI employees do and start a free trial. Primary action: 'Start free trial'. Direction: MindMarket 'warm storybook on cream paper' chosen by the owner on 2026-11-12 (replaces the 2026-11-11 Ember editorial style): owner's palette verbatim at the top of web/src/styles.css plus a semantic layer; Graphite text, Steel secondary, Brass accent text, Ember orange only for underlines and chart marks, square buttons, asymmetric feature cards, 20px white data cards on an Ash app canvas, pill nav, no shadows; headings Inter Tight 400 (PolySans substitute), body Inter. Hierarchy: hero headline + live product mockup first, then how it works, employees, control center, Slack, pricing, FAQ. Constraints: WCAG 2.2 AA, no framework, landing JS < 150 kB gz and CSS < 30 kB gz, max two web font families, target viewports 375x812, 768x1024, 1440x900. References: the owner's pasted editorial style reference (light, warm, data-card imagery). Quality review (2026-11-10): /review.html is the MAIZ platform owner's queue (noindex); specialised-task sign-off moved from the client to the platform owner. Owner admin (2026-11-10): /owner-specialists.html, /owner-clients.html and /owner-prices.html join /review.html behind a shared platform-owner menu (all noindex): custom specialists wait for the owner's approval and price, a clients table shows trial, setup, energy, AI cost and what is waiting, and a prices and packages page edits package prices, trial length, store prices and each agent's daily energy now or from a date, with history. AI spend (2026-11-10): /owner-ai.html (noindex, in the same owner menu) shows month spend against a Claude-only baseline, provider and budget meters, per-work and per-day tables, and editable models, pass marks and caps. Checked with axe at 375/768/1440 and by eye on screenshots with mocked data (the QA run itself shows the log-in gate). Batch queue (2026-11-10): /app.html#work gains a 'Waiting for the batch' panel (queued tasks, run now, cancel, closing-time form) and /owner-ai.html gains a batch queue panel, batch settings and batch savings tiles. Signup (2026-11-11): /onboarding.html now asks by tapping: kind of business (13 sector tiles), what the owner wants help with (10 needs, the sector's usual three pre-ticked with a dashed edge), apps already in use (the sector's usual apps first), then shows the plan built from those answers (who starts today and on what, who stands by, add-on offer, apps and how each connects, what was filled in) and asks for the email last. The plan comes from pure rules shared with the server, no AI call. The setup form in /app.html#setup arrives prefilled, each answer labelled 'From your signup answers' or 'Our guess'. Team energy pool (2026-11-11): Team package £100 a month with 8,000 energy a week shared by the team; extra employee £25 and specialist £35, each +2,000 a week; top-up packs that roll over with auto-reload off by default (Settings); energy shown as a share of the week; a compare-with-hiring calculator on the pricing page. HR desk and employee dashboards (2026-11-11): /app.html#people is the HR manager desk for the client's own staff (sector document rules, what needs doing, staff table, six-tab person record); /app.html#desk/<employee> is each AI employee's dashboard. Decisions (2026-11-11): /owner-decisions.html (noindex, first in the owner menu) lists every request waiting for the platform owner, oldest first; the one email the owner receives links to it. /owner-ai.html gains a GPU plan panel (recommended and current GPUs, finish time, estimated cost) and GPU settings; checked with axe at 375/768/1440, the QA run shows the log-in gate. Staff details form (2026-11-11): /staff-form.html#t=<link> is a member of staff's own noindex form (no account, no ID uploads), and the HR desk person record has an 'About them' tab with the same fields. Homepage round (2026-11-12): headlines use Fraunces (soft storybook serif, Google Fonts) with Inter for text, still two families. Homepage: hero with a tilted character collage and floating task notes, a moving ribbon, colour bento of the inside pages, a numbers strip, coloured team chips and a coral closing section with the team scene. The simulated demo band and every public 'Live demo' link are gone; outside localhost the control centre sends logged-out visitors to log in. The Employees page lists add-on roles as compact cards with a department filter instead of the full org blueprint. 'Questions, answered plainly' is now 'FAQs'. Logo, share preview and SEO (2026-11-12): the mark is a white M wearing a grass-green hat with a coral band on an Ink tile (favicon.svg, logo.png 512, apple-touch-icon 180, og.png 1200x630); every indexed page gets OG/Twitter tags, WebPage JSON-LD, breadcrumbs, robots allowing search and AI crawlers, a sitemap and llms.txt; the Solutions page has one section per sector built from the signup sector data. Connections (2026-11-14): /owner-connections.html (owner only, noindex) lets the platform owner connect Facebook Page, Instagram and WhatsApp from the browser and see/test Resend, Stripe, RunPod, Claude and Slack. Each card is asked for by the team member who needs it (avatar + 'Needed by'), with numbered tickable steps, deep links to Meta screens, fields (secrets never returned), Test connection, Disconnect, webhook URL/verify token to copy and a WhatsApp test message. Promotion agent, Community growth, Decisions and My AI team pages show a first-person 'what I need from you' bubble with status badges linking to the right card. Platform keys (2026-11-14): a 'For your clients' group (Google and Microsoft sign-in, Slack, Xero, Square) and Resend email are typed on the same page, encrypted, applied without a restart, each with 'What your clients get', redirect addresses to copy and a made-up-code test; Stripe, RunPod and Claude stay server settings.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core 4.10 (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa, wcag22aa, best-practice) reports 0 violations on /, /onboarding.html, /app.html, /app.html#setup, /app.html#team and /employees.html at 375, 768 and 1440 (npm run qa). Before this change it reported footer text contrast 3.97:1, skipped heading level in the footer, 79 nodes outside landmarks on the landing page and no main landmark in the app. Keyboard: first Tab focuses a visible 'Skip to content' link that moves focus to main; the mobile menu opens with the button, closes on Escape and returns focus to the button. All links, buttons, inputs and summaries are at least 24x24 px at 375 wide. Form errors use role=alert, aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and move focus to the field. Not covered: a screen-reader pass with VoiceOver or NVDA. Job descriptions (2026-11-10): the employees page had no h1 and the app's Team screen skipped from h2 to h4 and had a scrollable org chart that could not be focused; all three are fixed (h1 eyebrow, heading level passed to the job-description renderer, focusable labelled org-chart region). Job descriptions and blueprint roles are native details/summary elements, so they open with the keyboard. Combined release (2026-11-10): npm run qa now scans 17 pages and screens (every public page plus all ten control center screens) at 375, 768 and 1440: 51 checks, 0 axe violations, 0 overflow, 0 console errors, run against the real server with production headers. Not covered: a screen-reader pass with VoiceOver or NVDA.
